Durchlauchtigster Fürst
Gnädigster Fürst und Herr!
Aus dem mit heutiger Post abgehenden Schreiben Sr. Ma¬
jestät des Königs, werden Ew. hochfürstliche Durchlaucht des
mehren zu ersehen geruhen, wie Allerhöchst dieselben den
wahren Werth höchſt Dero SüdPreußischen Güter, und den
von Krotoszyn und Polajewo näher untersuchen laßen wolle.
um diese Besizzungen sodann gehörig gegen ein ander Ba¬
lanciren zu können, und kann höchst Denenselben ich gewiß
versichern, daß wenn dem intendirten Tausch nicht wichtige
hinderniße im Wege ſtehen, es Sr. Majestät den König zum
vergnügen gereichen wird, höchſt Dero dieſfälligen Wunsch
nachgekommen.
Für das huldreiche Vertrauen, welches Ew. Hochfürſtliche
Durchlaucht mir durch höchſt. Dero gnädigen Schreiben vom
7ten d. M. zu bezeigen geruhen, sage höchst-Denenſelben u.
den tief verpflichtesten Dank, und ob gleich die Sache ſelbſt
nicht durch meine Hände gehet, indem solche nicht in mein Fach

translation.en:
94

Most Serene Prince,

Most gracious Prince and Lord!

From the letter of His Majesty the King going out by today's post, Your Most Serene Highness will be pleased to perceive more fully how His Majesty is minded to have the true value of Your Serene Highness's South Prussian estates, and that of Krotoszyn and Polajewo, more closely examined, in order then to be able duly to balance these possessions one against the other; and I can assuredly assure Your Serene Highness that, if no weighty obstacles stand in the way of the intended exchange, it will afford His Majesty the King pleasure to have complied with Your Serene Highness's wish in this matter.

For the gracious confidence which Your Most Serene Highness is pleased to show me by Your Serene Highness's gracious letter of the 7th of this month, I offer Your Serene Highness [uncertain: my] most deeply obliged thanks; and although the matter itself does not pass through my hands, inasmuch as it does not fall within my

department, I shall nonetheless be no less glad to see it brought to Your Most Serene Highness's complete satisfaction, inasmuch as the heartfelt veneration I bear for Your Serene Highness assuredly makes me take the warmest part therein. Nothing in the world could only hereafter make happier than to be able to lay before Your Most Serene Highness the proofs of that true reverence with which I remain, until death, Your Most Serene Highness's Berlin,

the 18th of December

1798.

entirely most humble, faithful

and most obedient

Zastrow

Most Serene Prince,

Most gracious Prince and Lord!

From the letter of His Majesty the King going out by today's post, Your Most Serene Highness will be pleased to perceive more fully how His Majesty is minded to have the true value of Your Serene Highness's South Prussian estates, and that of Krotoszyn and Polajewo, more closely examined, in order then to be able duly to balance these possessions one against the other; and I can assuredly assure Your Serene Highness that, if no weighty obstacles stand in the way of the intended exchange, it will afford His Majesty the King pleasure to have complied with Your Serene Highness's wish in this matter.

For the gracious confidence which Your Most Serene Highness is pleased to show me by Your Serene Highness's gracious letter of the 7th of this month, I offer Your Serene Highness [uncertain: my] most deeply obliged thanks; and although the matter itself does not pass through my hands, inasmuch as it does not fall within my

department, I shall nonetheless be no less glad to see it brought to Your Most Serene Highness's complete satisfaction, inasmuch as the heartfelt veneration I bear for Your Serene Highness assuredly makes me take the warmest part therein. and most obedient

summary_en: Zastrow gives notice of a letter from the King going out with today's post: the King wishes to have the true value of the Prince's South Prussian estates and of Krotoszyn and Polajewo investigated, in order to weigh them against one another. If no important obstacles stand in the way of the intended exchange, he says the King will gladly grant the wish. Zastrow thanks him for the letter of the 7th of the month. He says the matter does not belong to his department, but that he hopes for a satisfactory conclusion.
summary_de: Zastrow kündigt ein mit heutiger Post abgehendes Schreiben des Königs an: Der König will den wahren Wert der südpreußischen Güter des Fürsten sowie von Krotoszyn und Polajewo untersuchen lassen, um sie gegeneinander abzuwägen. Stehen dem beabsichtigten Tausch keine wichtigen Hindernisse entgegen, werde der König den Wunsch gern erfüllen. Zastrow dankt für das Schreiben vom 7. des Monats. Die Sache gehöre nicht in sein Fach, er hoffe aber auf einen befriedigenden Abschluss.

reading.notes: Zastrow writes to the Prince from Berlin. He announces a letter from the King, sent by today's post: the King will have the true value of the Prince's South Prussian estates and of Krotoszyn and Polajewo examined so that they can be balanced against each other for the planned exchange. Zastrow assures the Prince that the King will gladly grant the wish if no important obstacles stand in the way. He thanks the Prince for his letter of the 7th. The matter does not pass through his hands because it is not in his department, but he hopes to see it settled to the Prince's satisfaction. Nothing in it concerns Trąbczyn directly.
